active_key_version.description:
The asymmetric crypto key version to use for signing approval requests.
Empty active_key_version indicates that a Google-managed key should be used for signing.
This property will be ignored if set by an ancestor of the resource, and new non-empty values may not be set.
active_key_version.rationale: This argument provides the customer-managed crypto key that is used to approve requests, empty would mean that google controls the key. By mandating a customer-managed key provides the organization with control over the signing material. Therefore, a policy must require it to be set.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: This argument determines if Terraform can delete the setting resource, Access Approval settings can be deleted because they are recreatable configurations. Therefore, false.

notification_emails.description:
A list of email addresses to which notifications relating to approval requests should be sent.
Notifications relating to a resource will be sent to all emails in the settings of ancestor
resources of that resource. A maximum of 50 email addresses are allowed.
notification_emails.rationale: This argument controls the emails that are notified when an approval request is received. The emails that an organization choses to use is determined by themselves, and there is no way a policy could determine if one email is safer than another. Therefore, false.

project.rationale: This argument operates as the project identifier, and is defaulted to the provider's project when ignored. This identifier is organization specific, and one broad policy can not constrain in. Therefore, false.

project_id.description: ID of the project of the access approval settings.
project_id.rationale: This argument determines which project the settings are applied to. Acting as a reference towards the project resources, and does not act as a security control. Therefore, false.

enrolled_services.description:
A list of Google Cloud Services for which the given resource has Access Approval enrolled.
Access requests for the resource given by name against any of these services contained here will be required
to have explicit approval. Enrollment can only be done on an all or nothing basis.

A maximum of 10 enrolled services will be enforced, to be expanded as the set of supported services is expanded.

enrolled_services.cloud_product.description:
The product for which Access Approval will be enrolled. Allowed values are listed (case-sensitive):
  all
  appengine.googleapis.com
  bigquery.googleapis.com
  bigtable.googleapis.com
  cloudkms.googleapis.com
  compute.googleapis.com
  dataflow.googleapis.com
  iam.googleapis.com
  pubsub.googleapis.com
  storage.googleapis.com
enrolled_services.cloud_product.rationale: Allow access to Google services depending on the project.

enrolled_services.enrollment_level.description: The enrollment level of the service. Default value: "BLOCK_ALL" Possible values: ["BLOCK_ALL"]
enrolled_services.enrollment_level.rationale: Ensure default value is already assigned to the enrollment level.
